intent: Verified customer demands release of £750 hold placed after an interbank APP-scam funds-recovery request; he asserts a genuine in-person van sale and needs rent money tomorrow.
summary: Keep the existing £750 hold (not broadened); the agent cannot release it while a live interbank recovery request is under bank policy. Refer urgently to H&V Fraud Operations with the customer's in-person collection account, his listing/chat exports, the unresolved conflict with the payer's statement, the 2-working-day Meridian deadline and the rent hardship. Ask the customer for the missing V5C/DVLA sale proof. Reply explaining the hold, what is undecided, and hardship support.

facts.claim: Caller passed ID&V on the phone channel and is the account holder Marcus Bell.
£2,600 Faster Payment credited 21 Sep 14:10 from L FARRELL (Meridian), ref VAN; £1,850 debited 21 Sep 16:40 to customer's own Barclaycard payee on file since 2022.

Meridian sent an interbank funds-recovery request (MER-FR-2026-081734) on 23 Sep 17:55 categorising the payment as purchase scam – vehicle not received; payer states seller promised delivery Tuesday; no police reference; no previous reports against the payee account.
System hold of £750 (all available funds) applied 23 Sep 17:56; bank policy is to hold the disputed amount still available and respond to the sending bank within 2 working days.
Customer asserts the buyer collected the van in person on Monday 21 Sep and paid by transfer on his drive; he says he has listing, messages and V5 handover evidence.

Customer-exported listing states collection only and marked SOLD 21 Sep; customer-exported chat shows buyer 'Lou F.' stating she was outside the address and sending payment ref VAN at 14:06, and the seller confirming keys/V5C green slip at 14:11. These are customer-supplied exports, not bank-verified records.
The payer's statement (delivery promised, no van) and the customer's evidence (in-person collection) directly conflict; the conflict is unresolved on the supplied records.
Customer states rent of £900 is due tomorrow (25 Sep); the held amount is £750, which is all available funds.
Customer has 6 years with the bank, no fraud markers, no other inbound credits from unknown parties in 90 days, no contact history in 12 months.
No solver tools or bank execution are connected; all steps are proposals.

missing: Fraud Operations decision on the hold and the response to Meridian (not yet made)
V5C/DVLA notification-of-sale evidence the customer says he holds (not in supplied attachments)
Whether marketplace buyer 'Lou F.' can be linked to payer L FARRELL (not established by bank records)
Individual event times for today's call (only day precision recorded)
Whether any other funds, income or standing orders are expected before rent is due

steps.instruction: Maintain the existing system hold of GBP 750.00 on account SYN-ACCT-01-1 (Marcus Bell) linked to recovery request MER-FR-2026-081734; decline the customer's request for immediate release at servicing-agent level. Scope: the £750 held only; do not extend to any other account function. Reason to record: active interbank APP-scam recovery request with an unresolved factual conflict; decision reserved to Fraud Operations under bank policy.

rationale.explanation: The hold was applied per stated bank policy on receipt of the Meridian request; the customer's evidence is credible but customer-supplied and directly contradicts the payer's statement, so the agent cannot safely lift it on the call. The hold must stay proportionate to the £750 already held.
rationale.criterion: Hold the identified disputed funds pending the responsible team's review; do not broaden a hold beyond the risky operation; name unresolved conflicts rather than guessing.

steps.target: Harrow & Vale Bank plc account hold (hold notice MER-FR-2026-081734)

steps.instruction: Refer case 001 urgently to Harrow & Vale Fraud Operations (addressee of the Meridian request) for a decision on the £750 hold and the reply to Meridian due within 2 working days of 23 Sep 17:55. Pass: Meridian ref MER-FR-2026-081734; customer's ID&V-passed account on 24 Sep that buyer collected the van in person on 21 Sep and paid by transfer on his drive; attachments customer_evidence_listing.txt (collection only, SOLD 21 Sep) and customer_evidence_messages.txt (buyer 'Lou F.' on site 13:52–14:12, payment ref VAN 14:06 matching credit 14:10); the conflict with the payer's 'delivery promised' statement; £1,850 spent to his own Barclaycard before the request; no fraud markers, 6-year relationship, no other unknown-party credits; hardship: £900 rent due 25 Sep with all available funds held. Ask Fraud Operations to prioritise given the rent deadline and to decide whether to retain, part-release or release the hold, and to notify the customer by his registered phone contact.

rationale.explanation: The recovery request is addressed to Fraud Operations and the hold decision and interbank response sit with them; the customer's hardship (essential living cost) and the contradictory evidence make an urgent, informed review the correct next move rather than any agent-level release or refusal.
rationale.criterion: Distinguish an authorised payment allegation from proof; a recovery request is not a completed return; refer essential-living-cost hardship to the appropriate team without blanket refusal.

steps.target: Harrow & Vale Bank plc Fraud Operations

steps.instruction: Ask Marcus Bell to send, via the bank's secure document upload or secure message (not by reading details over the phone), the V5C handover evidence he mentioned: the DVLA notification-of-sale confirmation (email/reference) or a copy of the completed V5C/2 new-keeper slip showing the buyer's details and 21 Sep date. Confirm the listing and chat exports already on file do not need re-sending.

rationale.explanation: The customer states he has V5 handover proof but it is not among the supplied attachments; it is the one item that could independently corroborate in-person collection and the buyer's identity for the Fraud Operations review.
rationale.criterion: Request only the specific missing fact that changes the decision; use a secure route for documents.

steps.instruction: Tell Marcus Bell on the call: 'I understand this is urgent with rent due tomorrow. Here is exactly what happened: on the evening of 23 September the bank that sent you the £2,600 raised a formal recovery request saying their customer reports that payment as a scam – a van paid for but not received. Our rules mean the system automatically held whatever was still available, which is the £750, while that request is reviewed. It is not a fraud marker against you and nothing else on your account is restricted. I can't release the £750 myself and I can't promise when or whether it will be released – that decision sits with our fraud team, who must respond to the other bank within 2 working days. What I am doing now is sending your account of the collection, your listing and your chat messages to that team today as evidence in your favour, flagging your rent deadline, and asking them to prioritise. Please send your V5C/DVLA sale confirmation through the secure upload so they have it too. I have to be straight with you: even if the full £750 were released it is less than your £900 rent, so it would help to speak to your landlord today. If this is going to leave you short on essentials, I can refer you to our financial support team.' Do not quote the other bank's customer's statement verbatim or share their account details.

rationale.explanation: The customer is verified and entitled to know why his funds are held, what is and is not decided, what he can do, and the realistic position on rent; the reply must stay within recorded facts and avoid promising release or outcome.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the recorded status and what it does not confirm; honour hardship with supportive handling; do not promise outcomes or timescales without evidence.

must_state: The £750 hold was applied automatically on 23 Sep because the sending bank raised a formal recovery request saying their customer reports the £2,600 van payment as a scam (goods not received)
Bank policy requires the available disputed funds to be held while the request is reviewed; the servicing agent cannot release it on the call
His account of in-person collection and his listing/chat exports are being passed to the bank's fraud team as evidence in his favour; the bank has not yet decided
The bank must respond to the sending bank within 2 working days of 23 Sep; no release outcome or timing can be promised
The hold applies only to the £750 held; it is not a fraud marker against him
Even if released, £750 is less than the £900 rent; the bank can refer him to its financial support team and he may wish to tell his landlord now
What one piece of evidence to send and how (V5C/DVLA sale confirmation via secure channel)
must_not: Do not promise or imply the £750 will be released, or give a release date or time
Do not state or imply the customer is a scammer, or that the Meridian payer is lying; the dispute is unresolved
Do not disclose the payer's account identifiers, Meridian case internals beyond the fact and nature of the dispute, or the payer's full statement verbatim
Do not broaden the hold beyond the £750 already held or suggest other account functions are restricted
Do not claim the agent can decide the hold; Fraud Operations owns the decision
Do not promise the bank will cover rent, offer high-cost borrowing, or promise any outcome of Meridian's claim
Do not claim any referral or review has already happened; steps are proposals pending execution
